events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven.** I'd expect boat salmon there to rate about **2 of 4 (average, with upside)**. Expected rating for the others: **South Haven 1, Muskegon 1, St. Joseph 1** (low confidence).
- Start around **90 to 120 ft** of water, or **70 to 80 ft** if the bite is inshore, and run lines **40 to 80 ft down**.
- Lures: glow or chrome J-plugs, glow spoons, and meat rigs. Add white flashers or flies.
- Check the wind before you go. I don't have a current wind forecast in these results.

## Why

- Grand Haven's newest boat report (Aug 30) rated the bite good (3), with fish 40 to 80 ft in 40 to 80 ft of water, and the report before it (Aug 16) also rated good.
- Muskegon and Grand Haven share the same buoy, but Muskegon's newest boat report (Aug 30) was slow (0), so I'd expect Muskegon to be a step behind.
- South Haven and St. Joseph had slow or unrated boat reports on Aug 30, and St. Joseph's boats mostly stayed in because of weather, so I'd expect neither to beat Grand Haven this week.
- I'd expect the bite to stay patchy, since the last four weeks have swung between good and slow at every port.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is 2023-08-30, about 6 days old)
- Grand Haven, Aug 30: boats rated good (3) in 40 to 80 ft of water. "Glow or chrome J-plugs worked well, along with white flasher/flies." Pier casting was below average (1).
- Grand Haven, Aug 23: boats rated slow (0) in 90 to 180 ft of water, fish 45 to 100 ft down, "Glow plugs, glow spoons and meat rigs all worked well."
- Grand Haven, Aug 16: boats rated good (3), "The best action was 40 to 90 down in 70 to 150 feet of water."
- Muskegon, Aug 30: boats rated slow (0) in 70 to 130 ft of water, fish 55 to 100 ft down. "Glow spoons, meat rigs and J-plugs seemed to work the best."
- Muskegon, Aug 16: boats rated good (3) with Chinook and coho, 30 to 80 ft down in 50 to 120 ft of water.
- South Haven, Aug 30: boats rated slow (0), though the text said "pretty good." The best water was 90 to 120 ft, and "meat rigs, rotators and flies seemed to catch the most fish."
- South Haven, Aug 16: boats rated good (3) at 80 to 100 ft, with rotators, flies and meat rigs.
- St. Joseph, Aug 30: boats not rated. "Due to poor weather, very few anglers made it out." Boats targeted 90 to 100 ft.
- St. Joseph, Aug 23: boats slow (0). "Salmon anglers had a hard time locating fish."

**Past seasons** (matched on similar water temperature, per the similar-weeks search)
- Late August at about 63 F in Grand Haven and Muskegon: both boat reports were slow (0). (Grand Haven and Muskegon, Aug 23, 2023)
- Early and mid September at about 70 F in South Haven and St. Joseph: boats rated average (2) in 2022, with fish at about 110 to 120 ft. (South Haven and St. Joseph, Sept 14 and 21, 2022)

**Conditions now** (buoy readings for the week before today; the tool returned a summary, not live data)
- Grand Haven and Muskegon (buoy 45161): average 63 F, up 12 F over the week. I'd expect this warm-up to mean the upwelling of late August has faded.
- South Haven (buoy 45168): average 68 F, up 5 F.
- St. Joseph (buoy 45026): average 71 F, up 4 F.
- The modeled cold-layer depth and pierhead readings were not returned, so I can't say where the 55 F to 58 F water sits.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from Aug 30, about 6 days old. Treat the ratings as a guide and check a fresh report before you go.
- The buoy readings are measured but offshore. The modeled cold-layer depth is missing, so depth advice relies on the reports.
- Grand Haven's good rating came after a sharp temperature drop. That warm-up this week may have ended it, which is why I rate it 2, not 3.
- General guidance (NY DEC, Michigan Sea Grant): Chinook and coho hold at 52 to 58 F, and cold water near shore pulls fish toward piers and river mouths when the wind is north or east. I didn't find a wind forecast, so I can't say whether that applies this week.
